subject: nahw
definition: Rafʿ, naṣb, khafḍ (also called jarr) and jazm. Nouns take the first three; verbs take rafʿ, naṣb and jazm.
explanation: Their basic signs are vowels: ḍamma for rafʿ (زَيْدٌ، يَنْصُرُ), fatḥa for naṣb (زَيْدًا، لَنْ يَنْصُرَ), kasra for khafḍ (بِزَيْدٍ) and sukūn for jazm (لَمْ يَنْصُرْ).

Some words show their state with letters instead of vowels: the dual, the sound masculine plural, the five nouns such as أَبُوكَ (your father), and the five verbs such as يَنْصُرُونَ. Al-Ājurrūmiyya gives each state its signs in turn.

examples.arabic: وَأَقْسَامُهُ أَرْبَعَةٌ: رَفْعٌ وَنَصْبٌ وَخَفْضٌ وَجَزْمٌ
examples.english: Its kinds are four: rafʿ, naṣb, khafḍ and jazm (al-Ājurrūmiyya).
lam yanṣur: jazm, which only verbs take.
